301.trigger: The client leans toward interpretation and judgment and finds it hard to state concrete feelings; immediate clues such as sadness, crying, anger, clenched fists, tone changes, and pauses appear on site.

302.skill_name: Point out and feed back in-session emotional and somatic cues
302.skill_description: When presently observing tension, restlessness, wandering gaze and other nonverbal and emotional signs, identify and feed back their intensity and expression difficulty in neutral language, inviting expanded and refined description, normalizing present feelings, helping the client stay in the present and deepening awareness.
302.when_to_use: When clear Anxiety or immediate emotional fluctuation appears in the session, when nonverbal clues need to be seen and used to deepen present experience.
302.trigger: Restlessness, tense rigidity, breathing changes, tone/manner/pace changes, lowness and pauses, repeatedly saying 'do not know', struggling to name emotions.

323.skill_name: Observe and record present nonverbal and verbal cues
323.skill_description: Upon entering the room and in dialogue, carefully observe and record the present clothing, facial expression, speech rate, tension level, emotional reactions, and verbal features (such as clarity of expression, pauses, hand-wringing), so as to grasp the current state and tension, serving as a basis for immediate understanding and intervention and tracking changes.
323.when_to_use: The present-state assessment at initial visit and at the start of each session, or continuous observation alongside conversation when discussing sensitive topics or emotional fluctuations.
323.trigger: In-session signals such as flat expression, slower speech rate, tension, gaze avoidance, pauses in speech, and hand-wringing.

240.skill_name: Feed back and follow up on current nonverbal changes
240.skill_description: Feed back the immediate on-site changes such as facial expressions and tone in neutral language, helping the client perceive the present state and its shifts, and in time follow up from this entry point to unfold the related content, making the present experience material that can be seen and explored, and pushing the dialogue in an effective direction.
240.when_to_use: When an observable change in facial expression or tone appears on site, or when a keyword is heard the client shows immediate reactions such as raising the head or a change of attention.
240.trigger: Immediate changes in expression and tone, raising/lowering the head, playing with fingers, and other small reactions; changes in attention to keywords such as 'confidentiality'.

281.skill_name: Empty-chair integration: venting again and connecting relational impact
281.skill_description: After empty-chair dialogue and role switching, Guidance the client to again vent growing dissatisfaction and distress, identifying other relationship influences behind parent-child conflict, expanding and deepening present awareness, for integration at the technique's end.
281.when_to_use: The integration segment at the end of the empty-chair technique, when awareness and understanding need to be deepened.
281.trigger: When unvented emotions remain or understanding of conflict causes is one-sided.

261.skill_name: Use the empty chair for present dialogue and reenactment
261.skill_description: Set two chairs in the counseling room, Guidance the client to dialogue in the present with significant others or self parts, rotating roles and reenacting conflicts on site, expressing Repressed emotions and needs, practicing perspective-taking and genuine communication, integrating inner conflict, enhancing presence, self-awareness and change.
261.when_to_use: When emotion is suppressed, interpersonal conflict is prominent, or cognition is rigid, it is necessary to bring historical events into the present experience or to practice communication and perspective-taking on site.
261.trigger: Persistent prejudice or strong emotion toward specific figures, blocked communication; talks about grief/separation/guilt fragments; produces self-contradiction and pulling over rejection methods or election failure.

282.skill_name: Negotiate and clarify short-term and long-term counseling goals
282.skill_description: Based on the assessment results and the client's needs, jointly negotiate and clarify near-term and long-term goals, ensuring the goals are clear, concrete and measurable (such as emotion/sleep/interpersonal/study, cognitive correction, self-acceptance and personality improvement); when necessary, integrate the expectations of parents and other parties and record them, unifying direction and expectations, as the basis for subsequent technique selection, planning and assessment.
282.when_to_use: After completing the initial assessment and diagnosis, entering the plan formulation and goal alignment stage; in early counseling or after the first session, when direction needs to be clarified.
282.trigger: The client has provided basic information and expressed motivation and expectations for improvement; the distress affects study and life, and the direction of change and evaluation standards need to be clarified.

227.skill_name: Select and explain counseling methods and negotiate the plan
227.skill_description: Combined with the causes of the problem and the assessment results, select and explain the counseling method and principles to be used (such as cognitive behavioral, rational emotive, client-centered, family therapy, relaxation training, etc.), clarify the effects and cooperation requirements; negotiate the implementation plan with the client, so that the path and arrangements reach agreement, raising cooperativeness and participation expectations.
227.when_to_use: At the counseling plan formulation stage; after initial assessment and psychological testing are completed, or the first-stage session needs to clarify methods and arrangements.
227.trigger: When the client needs to understand the therapeutic method, does not understand the method and process or asks about concrete practices; needing to raise cooperation and practice motivation.

275.skill_name: Arranges processes and tasks in phases and sets evaluation nodes
275.skill_description: Divide the counseling into stages such as diagnostic assessment/relationship building - psychological help - consolidation and ending, clarifying each stage's goals, methods and homework feedback; arrange the number and rhythm of sessions (such as the first two for diagnosis, the middle eight for help, the last two for ending); summarize at each stage, check homework and feedback, set assessment nodes, revise the plan when necessary and discuss the timing of the ending.
275.when_to_use: Used when formulating the overall treatment plan and process; after the plan is determined it runs throughout, with focused implementation at stage transitions or the ending.
275.trigger: When needing to clarify the counseling process, frequency and phases; the client is unclear about the process and expectations or counseling enters a new phase, needing to review and consolidate existing gains.

309.skill_name: Arranges session purposes, number of sessions, and evaluation methods in phases
309.skill_description: Clarify the three-stage plan and rhythm (such as 1-4 building and assessment, 5-10 working, 11-13 review and ending), set progressive purposes and methods for each session; agree to assess the effects against the goals using the client's self-assessment, the counselor's observation and evaluations by people around them, facilitating tracking and revision.
309.when_to_use: At the point after the goal is determined and process arrangement begins; before the plan is implemented, when the session structure and evaluation method need to be clarified.
309.trigger: The client asks about counseling arrangements or needs a clear time structure; both sides have determined goals and methods and need to concretize the session rhythm and agree on measurement standards.

283.skill_name: Select and explain specific techniques and intervention paths
283.skill_description: According to the assessment and goals, select and explain the principles and steps of techniques such as emotional venting, cognitive behavioral, the empty chair, solution-focused, client-centered, rational emotive, mindfulness and relaxation, clarify their uses and applicability, making the client understand and reach a consensus, matching stage tasks and individual characteristics.
283.when_to_use: When formulating the plan and determining the treatment path; at the informed communication stage before implementing specific techniques.
283.trigger: When the problem nature and goals are clarified, needing to determine the concrete Intervention path; the client questions or expects regarding methods and process, or irrational beliefs and expression difficulties exist.

244.skill_name: Select and integrate orientations and method combinations to match goals
244.skill_description: Based on the assessment and diagnosis, select and integrate orientations and method combinations such as cognitive behavioral, client-centered, rational emotive, psychoanalytic or supportive psychotherapy, or clarify a person-centered orientation and core strategies; explain the core conditions and applicability to the client, reaching a consistent path and expectations.
244.when_to_use: When formulating the plan and pathway after completing the initial assessment; when the plan is being determined or advanced and the method orientation needs to be clarified.
244.trigger: When materials and tests are collected; clues like irrational beliefs, longing to be understood or function affected by triggering events exist, needing to choose and Interpretation main methods to establish agreement.

304.skill_name: Set and agree on counseling frequency, duration, and total number of sessions
304.skill_description: Jointly discuss with the client a fixed weekly time slot and duration (such as once a week, 50-60 minutes each time), clarify the total number of sessions or continuous cycle (such as 4-8 sessions or six weeks), dynamically discuss and adjust when necessary; inform about arrangements such as location and fees, forming a stable rhythm, facilitating execution, tracking and assessment.
304.when_to_use: After goals are determined, when concrete counseling arrangements need to be implemented; at the first session or plan confirmation and schedule negotiation stage; when signing the setting initially or needing to adjust frequency and duration during the process.
304.trigger: When both parties' time allows and continuity and predictability need ensuring; the client is unclear about arrangements or needs scheduling and structured arrangement; resources limited or short-term goals feasible.

236.skill_name: Explain the counseling setting, rules, and schedule
236.skill_description: In the first or early sessions, clearly explain the counseling setup and process to the client, including frequency and duration, location and fees, interaction style and basic rules, establishing session rhythm and Anticipation, reducing uncertainty and misunderstanding, facilitating subsequent assessment and cooperation.
236.when_to_use: At the first interview or early in counseling, when a basic framework and direction need to be established and follow-up arrangements clarified.
236.trigger: When the client first visits, unclear about process, rules or time frequency and fees, actively asking or expressing confusion.

278.skill_name: Jointly agree on and explain counseling goals and plans
278.skill_description: After collecting basic materials and initial assessment, discuss and establish phased and overall counseling goals with the client, explaining the intended therapy and steps, so they agree on direction and method, forming clear Anticipation, enhancing participation and cooperation.
278.when_to_use: After the 1st-2nd counseling sessions complete data collection and initial evaluation, the relationship preliminarily established, when assessment needs to be turned into goals and plans.
278.trigger: The client has stated her distress, expressed expectations or change motivation, asks about counseling direction and methods, preparing to negotiate goals and plans.

289.skill_name: Explain the client-centered approach and role positioning
289.skill_description: Clarify that the client is the expert on their own problems, the counselor assists their exploration as companion and facilitator, following the non-directive stance, not instilling values, helping them express and realize at their own pace, Clarification expectations and methods.
289.when_to_use: In the first Evaluative session or at the start of relationship building, when explaining methods and Clarification expectations.
289.trigger: When the client is uncertain about the counseling approach, expects direct guidance or worries the problem is too childish.

251.skill_name: Negotiate and establish goals and plans and confirm orientation fit
251.skill_description: After completing initial assessment, jointly agree on short-term and long-term goals and implementation plans with the client, Interpretation the intended therapy and principles, Clarification what can and cannot be done and making vagueappeals feasible, confirming their acceptance of and fit with the method and timeline.
251.when_to_use: At the early-stage fit assessment and goal clarification stage, after the assessment is completed and basic trust is established.
251.trigger: When the client is willing to collaborate, proposes expectations or asks about methods and timelines; goals still unclear or unrealistic, needing clear direction.

320.skill_name: Introduce the nature of counseling and confidentiality principles and rules
320.skill_description: In the first session, introduce the nature, meaning and limitations of counseling, explaining related matters and session rules, clarifying the confidentiality principle and boundaries, helping the client understand safety and Anticipation, lowering concerns and Anxiety, facilitating genuine expression and cooperation.
320.when_to_use: At the opening of the first session or the structured explanation stage, when it is necessary to clarify basic counseling information.
320.trigger: When the client understands counseling insufficiently, asks about process or privacy protection, appearing hesitant and uneasy.

224.skill_name: Explain that the client takes the lead and the counselor's role
224.skill_description: Clarify the principle of 'starting with the client's choice', explaining they will sit with a label and speak in first person; the counselor observes and records peripherally without joining the dialogue, only giving process prompts when needed, to help them express at their own pace.
224.when_to_use: The role and rule clarification segment before the formal start.
224.trigger: The client seeks direction: 'where should I start first' 'will you talk with me'.

259.skill_name: Explaining the counseling attitude and relationship conditions
259.skill_description: Introduce the counselor's attitude and relationship conditions: empathic understanding, unconditional positive regard and genuine consistent feedback, explaining these will promote the client's Free expression and Self-exploration, creating an understanding, supportive and respectful counseling relationship, helping them engage in the session at ease.
259.when_to_use: When setting expectations at the start, or when the client is uncertain about the counseling approach and role division.
259.trigger: When the client asks how it will proceed, whether they will be judged, or is unclear about the counselor's approach.

290.skill_name: Explain the counseling methods, process, and technical features
290.skill_description: Systematically introduce the adopted counseling orientation and methods, explaining the overall process and technical features, like active Listening, emotion and content reflection, Clarification and open-ended Questioning, helping the client understand how sessions proceed and the Anticipation path, building common understanding.
290.when_to_use: At the structure and method introduction step of the first or early sessions, before entering concrete techniques.
290.trigger: The client feels unfamiliar with or confused about the counseling process and methods, proactively asking about principles and ways.

279.skill_name: Explains and negotiates session time, frequency, and phase arrangements
279.skill_description: Clarify the session count, frequency and duration, as well as phase tasks and pace (like diagnosis—help—consolidation), and agree on fixed time slots, location and fees; when conflicts arise, negotiate adjustments in advance, making the process transparent and predictable, facilitating stable participation.
279.when_to_use: At the start of counseling or the plan-establishment stage, when the schedule and overall progress need clarifying.
279.trigger: When the client asks about time, frequency, fees or phase arrangements, unclear about duration and count.

270.skill_name: Explain the structure and steps of each session
270.skill_description: Clarify the basic structure and steps of a single session, e.g., first read the letter aloud, then discuss key information, the counselor analyzes the problem, and finally jointly analyze the self state, clarifying the process and role division, helping align the session rhythm.
270.when_to_use: When starting or transitioning to the letter-writing segment, needing to align the specific process and rhythm.
270.trigger: When the client is unclear about concrete steps, asking about the process or showing confusion.

295.skill_name: Explains confidentiality principles and exceptions and obtains informed consent
295.skill_description: At the start of the first or early sessions, clearly explain the confidentiality principle and exceptions, informing of recording and information use boundaries, responding to and Clarification the client's doubts; after answering, obtain written informed consent (including recording consent, etc.), to establish a safe and trusting cooperation basis.
295.when_to_use: At the launch phase of first sessions or when establishing the cooperation framework, when recording and information use need clear boundaries.
295.trigger: When the client first visits, asking about privacy protection or harboring doubts and unease about recording and material use.

305.skill_name: Agree on and explain counseling frequency, duration, and fees
305.skill_description: Jointly agree with the client on fixed time slots, frequency and each session's duration (like once weekly, about 50–60 minutes), and clarify total count and fees or free information and location, so they grasp the time rhythm and resource arrangement, reducing uncertainty and raising participation.
305.when_to_use: At the start of counseling or when formulating the plan, when the schedule and pace need to be clarified; when the client asks about time or fees.
305.trigger: The weekly counseling frequency, fixed time, duration, or fee needs to be determined with the client, or the client has doubts about the arrangement.

314.skill_name: Encourage the client's Free expression and create a non-judgmental atmosphere
314.skill_description: Clearly invite the client to freely narrate emotions and experiences at their own pace, emphasizing the counselor will accompany with accepting and non-judgmental attitude, allowing positive and negative emotions to fully present; explain when necessary that this session's pace centers on venting, lowering defensiveness and pressure, promoting open expression and Self-exploration.
314.when_to_use: At the early counseling and early exploration stage, used to create a safe, open atmosphere for expression; throughout, whenever emotional expression needs to be promoted.
314.trigger: When the client appears reserved or hesitant, Represses emotions, is Silent or worries about being evaluated, actively expressing Anxiety, irritability and other distress.

269.skill_name: Explain confidentiality rules and ethical boundaries and obtain consent
269.skill_description: In the first session, explain in detail the confidentiality principle and exceptions, ethical Demands and information use boundaries, signing or confirming a confidentiality agreement with the client and completing informed consent, alleviating insecurity and guardedness, building trust, promoting engagement and genuine expression.
269.when_to_use: At the setting step of the first consultation or before entering assessment, when boundaries need clarification and safety established.
269.trigger: When the client has concerns about privacy and confidentiality, appears guarded, or counseling will involve sensitive content.

229.skill_name: Explaining confidentiality exceptions and completing notification and coordination in high-risk situations
229.skill_description: At first contact or when assessment shows high risk like suicide, fully Interpretation the confidentiality agreement and possible confidentiality-breach situations, clarifying when the school or family needs informing; after obtaining the client's informed consent, conduct necessary risk feedback and linkage, enhancing the sense of safety and control.
229.when_to_use: At first contact and when assessed as high risk; when the client is unclear about confidentiality boundaries or worries about parents knowing.
229.trigger: When the client asks about confidentiality showing hesitation or refusing continued counseling; assessment shows high suicide risk needing linked Intervention.

288.skill_name: Empathically follow and reflect present experience
288.skill_description: Being present with genuineness and respect, patiently Listening and staying close to the client's narration, jointly describing their present language, behavior and emotions; through asking and reflecting, helping more clearly identify thedistress source, feelings and meaning, feeding back understanding, facilitating trust, relaxation and deeper disclosure.
288.when_to_use: In the relationship-building and consolidation phase, especially in early sessions and when emotions are evoked; when narration is vague or emotions not yet named, needing to be understood and accepted.
288.trigger: When the client pauses, is Silent or uses vague words to describe 'interference', 'bad thoughts'; expressing painful experiences, lowness or self-deprecation like 'terrible', longing to be understood yet resisting being analyzed.

313.skill_name: Guiding narration and clarifying problems in depth
313.skill_description: With gentle guidance, prompt the client to proactively narrate the current confusion, growth experiences, and details; after a preliminary understanding, cooperatively explore the formation and maintaining factors of the distress, carry out dialogue centering on stress-release and relaxation paths, jointly clarify the problem, and enhance their experience of being understood and supported.
313.when_to_use: The early data collection and relationship-building stage; or after the first assessment, entering the second stage needing to deepen the relationship and clarify the problem.
313.trigger: The client's narrative is scattered or she is shy; she has a preliminary description of the distress but is still confused, and expresses hope to learn stress-reduction or relaxation methods.

234.skill_name: Affirm and encourage efforts, strengths, and insights
234.skill_description: Give concrete, genuine affirmation and encouragement for the client's active thinking and Self-exploration, positive behaviors and traits and new insights; combined with resource reflection, correcting self-deprecation, enhancing self-efficacy, confidence and cooperation motivation, consolidating the relationship and supporting their continued expression and attempt at Intervention.
234.when_to_use: When the client begins concretizing problems, attempting classification or Self-exploration; when self-evaluation is negative or feeding back homework, progress, strengths and resources.
234.trigger: When the client proposes difficulties but is willing to cooperate and begins recalling and summarizing their own experience; Self-denial or focusing only on the negative, or sharing progress and strengths like taking medication on time, regular exercise, actively booking appointments.

280.skill_name: Affirm and Reinforce willingness to actively seek help
280.skill_description: Recognize and Reinforce the client's willingness to actively seek help, taking it as the positive premise of Establishing the counseling relationship, promoting the formation of trust and cooperation with concrete encouragement and affirmation.
280.when_to_use: At the start of the session or the initial contact stage, used to quickly build cooperation and trust.
280.trigger: The client proactively seeks help from a school counselor or clearly expresses a help-seeking need.

226.skill_name: Respectful Listening and unconditionally accepting Empathic response
226.skill_description: Focused, patient and with unconditional acceptance, Listen to the client's experiences and emotions, giving Empathy and understanding responses, and feeding back their feelings and meaning in accurate language; normalizing stress and Anxiety, conveying being seen and understood, building trust and deepening the counseling relationship.
226.when_to_use: At the diagnostic stage of the first session and sessions 1-2, and in the third session as the relationship deepens; when the client expresses distress or emotional fluctuation.
226.trigger: When crying, unease, insomnia, reduced appetite, hostility and other signals appear; listless, voice low; recounting pain, tension, Anxiety, fear or emptiness, or oversensitive to evaluation with self-blame.

307.skill_name: Communicate effectively, inquire, and honestly admit uncertainty
307.skill_description: Through clear, patient communication and targeted inquiry, help clarify the client's main problems and causes; when the session stalls or the path is unclear, the counselor honestly admits mistakes or uncertainty and invites joint exploration, modeling cooperation and integrity, strengthening trust and the Work alliance.
307.when_to_use: During first-phase relationship building and data collection; or when the session hits difficulties, and the period when choosing experiment or Intervention paths is unclear.
307.trigger: When the client is willing to actively seek help and states actively but mutual trust is still insufficient; interaction stagnates, signs of the client questioning or Relationship tension appear.

265.skill_name: Negotiate and establish the counseling plan and interview matters
265.skill_description: After basic trust is established, negotiate and confirm the counseling plan together with the client, clarifying goals and paths; at the initial stage agree on the cooperation method, boundaries, and procedures, raising transparency and a sense of control, forming participation and commitment, and providing a relational basis for consistent action in later intervention.
265.when_to_use: Used after the initial evaluation is completed and the relationship is stable, upon entering the plan formulation stage; at the first and early sessions, when a cooperative relationship and boundaries need to be established.
265.trigger: Needing to clarify concrete matters such as counseling arrangements, goal expectations, recording, and supervision; the client is willing to continue counseling and expresses a desire to change, willing to cooperate with related arrangements.

292.skill_name: Open-ended Questioning and Clarification promote Self-exploration
292.skill_description: Invite the client to describe feelings, meanings and needs with open-ended Questioning, Guidance their Free expression and refining of distress, avoiding Guidance and judgment; through Clarificationsorting out main problems, emotion sources, behavioral presentations and timelines, exploring willingness to change, deepening understanding and consolidating the Work alliance.
292.when_to_use: In the early-middle stage when expression needs to be expanded and understanding deepened; the intake conversation and information collection stage, exploring problems and motivation.
292.trigger: When the client's narration is vague or one-sided, sinking into self-reproach or unclear about self-needs; main problems and change motivation not yet clearly expressed, needing Clarification of emotion sources, behavioral presentations and timelines.

256.skill_name: Flexibly use open and closed inquiries to collect information
256.skill_description: Flexibly combine open and closed questions, systematically collect detailed data such as mental state and social functioning, expand the information surface and improve dialogue quality, promote effective communication and cooperation, and lay an empirical foundation for building trust and working together.
256.when_to_use: The assessment, diagnosis, and relationship-building stage, when needing to systematically understand the problem.
256.trigger: When the client narrates little on their own, answers briefly or shows long Silence, information insufficient, or descriptions of the problem remain general, key details missing.

262.skill_name: Identify and affirm self-resources, fostering self-support
262.skill_description: Work with the client to sort out things already accomplished such as growth and past organizational communication, light up inner strengths such as persistence, effort, tenacity, insight and executive ability, name and list strategies they can use autonomously, and give concrete affirmation; encourage practicing stating needs, controlling emotions, and reasonably declining at work, gradually returning the capacity to bear and regulate to themselves, reducing excessive dependence on others and on counseling.
262.when_to_use: In the mid-to-late counseling or conceptualization and goal-setting phase, when emotions stabilize, some safety has been gained and self-worth and ability exploration begins, preparing to Reinforce self-support.
262.trigger: When the client Self-denies, or begins recalling success experiences and strengths; showing persistence, Reflection, quick execution and other signs; describing being able to voice needs, control emotions or reasonably refuse non-duty tasks.

284.skill_name: Identify and mobilize Social support resources, planning external support
284.skill_description: Through Presuppositional questions, Approval and Exception questions, uncover existing and potential social and real support resources; jointly sort out usable support relationships and resources in life with the client, clarifying their sources and use, and in counseling connecting or finding other resources and support with encouragement, summaries and plans, reducing helplessness and single dependence on counseling.
284.when_to_use: In the assessment or closing phase, or the summary and planning phase after emotional improvement, when Weak social support or Intervention needs external support cooperation.
284.trigger: Self-reporting lack of family support, unable to use surrounding support systems or expressing helplessness and isolation; feeling uncertain about ending counseling or future problems while talking about obtainable help and relationships; beginning to express ability to fightdifficulties, continuing Self-exploration and finding support.

263.skill_name: Creating a safe and equal counseling relationship and providing transitional support
263.skill_description: With unconditional positive regard, Empathy, genuineness and active Listening, following and jointly describing their language, behavior and feelings, actively building an equal, open, expression-allowing atmosphere, providing reliable interpersonal support to promote venting and stability; when they show relationship improvement or self-support behaviors, giving genuine encouragement and emotional feedback, consolidating supported and self-affirmed experience, gradually extending self-support into life.
263.when_to_use: In the early session and relationship development and consolidation phase, for building a holding atmosphere and safety, stabilizing emotions, or when the client shows positive change and resource use needing consolidated support experience.
263.trigger: When the client appears dependent on the counselor, hoping for direct results, or self-reports lacking confidence, needing safety; unable to feel connection, fearing loss or expressing hesitation; tense, flat expression, Low mood, or reporting asking classmates for help, confiding in roommates, relationship improvement, on-site emotional loosening.

267.skill_name: Guiding disclosure to gain external support
267.skill_description: Guidance the client to confide in teachers, classmates or relatives and friends, and openly accept comforting and critical feedback; through full disclosure and external information feedback, alleviating tension, Anxiety and other emotions, correcting irrational cognitions, and as short-term external support prompting them to explore and connect with others.
267.when_to_use: When the client cannot dispel negative emotions alone, needing others' support and feedback.
267.trigger: When tension, Anxiety, insomnia appear, or expressing strong urges to vent and cry.

319.skill_name: Acceptance, Listening and Empathy provide emotional support
319.skill_description: In the session, creating a safe atmosphere with acceptance and non-judgment, attending to and responding to the client's feelings, actively Listening and Empathy their 'powerlessness, fatigue, dryness' and other experiences, creating a warm inclusive expressive space, as the core of environmental support to stabilize emotions and promote engagement.
319.when_to_use: Used throughout counseling, especially in early relationship building and emotional surges, or when they express grievance, Anxiety and self-blame, talking about family upheavals and vulnerable topics.
319.trigger: Worrying about being judged, expressing being slighted and Loneliness; sighing frequently, describing states with negative words, seeking professional support and comfort; nonverbal pain signals like furrowed brows, quiet voice, daring not to look directly, tears.

245.skill_name: Assess the support system and social functioning from multiple information sources
245.skill_description: Based on the intake interview and detailed data collection, using registration forms, confidentiality statements and psychological tests, combined with counselor reports and in-room observation, systematically sorting out the current state and gaps of family, interpersonal and campus support; also collecting information on Learning, relationships, family contact and sleep, and recording weak points related to interpersonal distress, to set goals and subsequent Intervention plans.
245.when_to_use: In the assessment and diagnosis stage of the initial visit, and the review before and after setting the counseling goals, when the influence of the support system on the current interpersonal trouble and the currently usable resources and weak links need to be determined.
245.trigger: When the client describes a discordant relationship with roommates, Loneliness, or past experiences lacking family/school support; presenting adaptation difficulties, Interpersonal alienation or family-care absence clues; social-function impairment signals like Reduced socializing, impaired Learning or Work, insomnia, or their own narrated information insufficient needing corroboration.

266.skill_name: Provide integrated feedback, monitor, and consolidate the adjusted support system
266.skill_description: Continuously collecting and comparing the client's self-report, counselor observation and peer, Teacher reports, monitoring symptom and functional changes, to judge whether Social support intervention is effective, and accordingly consolidating or adjusting the support system.
266.when_to_use: At the follow-up and effect evaluation stage, when whether the support system is effective and needs adjustment must be judged.
266.trigger: Evaluations from people around and school situation information are available, or symptom/function changes need external verification.

235.skill_name: Explain confidentiality and the counseling setting to establish safe boundaries
235.skill_description: At the first session or the preparation stage, explain the counseling setup (time, place, duration, fees) and common knowledge and rules of psychological counseling, clarify confidentiality principles and the exceptions to confidentiality, and explain recording and that supervision will be informed; sign with the client the informed consent, confidentiality agreement and life-safety commitment, providing a stable and predictable safety framework, reducing tension and concerns, and fostering cooperation and a sense of being supported.
235.when_to_use: Before the first session or the start of treatment, or whenever a new topic involves privacy and records, used to establish or consolidate a safe atmosphere and clear boundaries.
235.trigger: When first-time visitors are tense, uneasy or have concerns about the counseling process and confidentiality; worrying about privacy, skeptical of psychotherapy or not highly cooperative; large emotional fluctuations, with self-injury words or behavior clues or others reporting risk.

317.skill_name: Giving feedback and clarifying self-assessment results
317.skill_description: After completing the self-rating scales, feed the scores and corresponding levels back to the client (such as mild depression), clarify the meaning of the results in combination with their statements to avoid misunderstanding, promote alignment of the motivation for entering counseling and the goals, and provide a reference for later conceptualization and plan setting.
317.when_to_use: After scale administration, before the first comprehensive assessment and case conceptualization are formed.
317.trigger: Standard scores of scales obtained and the level and meaning need to be understood; the client raises questions about the meaning of results or shows confusion.

316.skill_name: Explain and administer self-rating scales to establish a baseline
316.skill_description: At the initial assessment stage, explain the testing purpose and scope, guide independently and truthfully completing the SCL-90, the depression self-rating scale and so on, standardize recording the scores and key indicators, assess the emotions and symptoms of the past week, forming an objective baseline, for subsequent case conceptualization, goal setting and efficacy assessment.
316.when_to_use: At the first or early session of case assessment, used to establish an objective baseline of emotions and symptoms; or when quantitative comparison is needed at post-treatment assessment and symptom fluctuation.
316.trigger: When the client first visits and agrees to assessment, complaining of depression, Anxiety and other symptoms needing quantified assessment; or planning periodic assessment, the client self-reporting Symptom improvement or worsening.

243.skill_name: Schedule and administer scales such as the SCL-90
243.skill_description: At the initial assessment and diagnosis stage, arrange and implement self-rating scales such as the SCL-90 and SAS, guide completion, standardize recording the total score, total mean score, number of positive items and factor scores, conduct initial screening and staged (before/after treatment, follow-up) assessment, establishing a baseline of psychological state, providing a basis for subsequent diagnosis and plans.
243.when_to_use: In the assessment, diagnosis and relationship-building phase of the first counseling, for obtaining a psychological baseline; or when Intervention effects and follow-up stability need testing.
243.trigger: When the client complains of depression, Anxiety, poor sleep, poor concentration and other symptoms needing quantified assessment; entering the treatment process or reaching the 3-month post-treatment follow-up node.

306.skill_name: Record and explain scale scores and severity levels
306.skill_description: After completing the testing, record each scale's scores and factor scores, based on the grading standards explain the severity (such as SDS 65 moderate, SAS 70 severe), clarify the problem level and nature, providing a basis for subsequent counseling goals and plan formulation, and clarify the clinical meaning of the results to the client or team.
306.when_to_use: After the assessment ends, when a preliminary judgment needs to be formed, severity delineated, and the plan-setting stage entered.
306.trigger: The obtained scale score indicates reaching the corresponding level or approaching the upper limit, and the chief complaint has affected study, social life, and daily living; the level and conclusion need to be given in the record.

322.skill_name: Integrate scale and clinical information to form an initial diagnostic judgment
322.skill_description: Analyze scale scores comprehensively together with the chief complaint, symptom duration, social functioning, and mental status examination, and refer to the 'three principles for distinguishing illness from non-illness' to judge the nature of the problem, avoiding conclusions based on scales alone, forming a preliminary diagnosis such as moderate depression, used to formulate counseling goals and follow-up plans.
322.when_to_use: After completing the assessment and collecting the medical history, when a preliminary diagnosis and a definition of the problem's nature need to be formed to guide plan formulation.
322.trigger: The SDS shows a moderate or higher score consistent with clinical observation and the chief complaint; the client provides life events and the chief complaint, and the mental status examination is completed.

255.skill_name: Feeds back and interprets SCL-90 results to formulate a plan
255.skill_description: After assessment, clearly Interpretation each SCL-90 factor score and degree (like depression, Anxiety, interpersonal sensitivity, paranoia), connecting the client's chief complaint and experience, summarizing main distress areas, and integrating Scale results with observation and interview materials, negotiating counseling goals and methods, providing objective reference.
255.when_to_use: After the pre-test is completed and the scale report is obtained, when the results need to be fed back to the client and a brief conclusion formed at the assessment and diagnosis segment.
255.trigger: The assessment shows moderate or abnormal factor scores; the client is confused about the meaning of the results or objective results need to be used for diagnostic judgment and plan formulation.

238.skill_name: Organize and compare scale changes across time points
238.skill_description: Organize the pre-treatment, post-treatment and follow-up SCL-90 total scores and key factor scores, carry out comparison and trend analysis, quantify the magnitude of symptom reduction, and collect subjective reports (such as self-feeling and life satisfaction) and place them in comparison, providing an objective basis for efficacy assessment and subsequent plans.
238.when_to_use: After completing scale assessments at each time point, when preparing to summarize outcomes or formulate subsequent treatment and follow-up plans.
238.trigger: Multi-time-point scale scores obtained; the client proactively feeds back experience changes or objective assessment results need to be fed back to the client / team.

297.skill_name: Re-administer and compare scales to assess outcomes
297.skill_description: In the ending or follow-up phase, re-administer previously used Scales (like SAS, SDS, SCL-90), comparing pre-post total scores, positive item counts and factor score changes, recording follow-up scores and comparing with initial or norm data, judging the improvement magnitude in Anxiety, depression and other dimensions, as Counseling effectiveness evaluation mutually corroborating subjective improvement experience.
297.when_to_use: At phase summaries, case-closing assessment or scheduled follow-up nodes, for testing Intervention effectiveness and Symptom improvement magnitude.
297.trigger: When Intervention is basically complete or counseling nears its end; the client feeds back improved state or needs objective testing; reaching the post-treatment follow-up node.

285.skill_name: Administers and interprets SDS/SAS to establish an emotional baseline
285.skill_description: In the assessment phase, selecting reliable and valid SDS, SAS (or SES), guiding the client to complete self-rating (can be done online), calculating total and standard scores, and determining depression/Anxiety severity, normatively recording results, establishing an emotional baseline, providing quantified basis for diagnosis, goal negotiation and risk identification.
285.when_to_use: In the first session or assessment phase, or when the crisis Intervention initial phase needs quantifying depression/Anxiety levels and establishing a baseline; when a baseline needs establishing before online counseling.
285.trigger: When the client reports Low mood, insomnia, despair or suicide ideation, accompanied by Anxiety and somatization clues; or expresses wanting objective reference and has agreed to assessment.

321.skill_name: Explain confidentiality and exceptions and obtain informed consent
321.skill_description: Before implementing the scales, explain the purpose, process, and requirements of the test, clarify the confidentiality principles and the exceptions to breaking confidentiality, elucidate the rights and obligations of both parties, respond to the client's doubts and sign the informed consent before entering the formal assessment, ensuring ethics, compliance, and cooperation.
321.when_to_use: Before counseling and assessment begin, when preparing to carry out standardized scale assessment or data collection.
321.trigger: The client's first visit or concerns about privacy and assessment; planning to implement tests such as SCL-90, SDS, and SAS and needing to obtain explicit informed consent.

232.skill_name: Administer and Interpretation SAS Anxiety level
232.skill_description: In the first assessment, guiding completion of the SAS Anxiety self-rating, calculating raw and standard scores, recording scores and Interpretation Anxiety degree by standard scores (like mild/moderate), establishing a quantified baseline, providing reference for subsequent Intervention and effect evaluation.
232.when_to_use: When the diagnostic assessment phase needs understanding the Anxiety baseline; or retesting in the ending consolidation phase to compare efficacy.
232.trigger: When the client presents tense unease, Fear, poor attention, chest tightness, insomnia and other Anxiety clues, needing Anxiety quantification.

271.skill_name: Incorporate SAS results into problem conceptualization
271.skill_description: Combined with the first consultation record and SAS scores, as one basis for defining the client's Anxiety degree, assisting in forming a conceptualization like 'Anxiety caused by adjustment disorder', and accordingly negotiating goals and choosing Intervention paths.
271.when_to_use: After completing the initial evaluation, discusses the nature of the problem with the client and formulates counseling goals and a plan together.
271.trigger: SAS scores obtained and a preliminary clinical impression formed; need to integrate objective quantitative results with subjective narration.

296.skill_name: Explain confidentiality and sign an agreement to promote assessment cooperation
296.skill_description: Before beginning testing and registration, clearly explain the confidentiality rules and the exceptions to breaking confidentiality, obtain informed consent and sign the confidentiality agreement, respond to doubts, reduce defensiveness and resistance, prompt at-ease cooperation with testing and data collection, and ensure the validity of the assessment and privacy safety.
296.when_to_use: In the diagnostic phase of the first two consultations, before starting psychological tests and data collection, or when crisis Intervention begins needing normative process and boundaries.
296.trigger: When the client has concerns about counseling or assessment, cooperativeness not high; about to provide personal information and complete psychological tests.

273.skill_name: Express and convey unconditional positive regard and acceptance
273.skill_description: Not judging the client's emotions, narration and real needs, respecting and accepting their contradictions and difficulties, genuinely caring and conveying the experience of being respected and included; in a safe atmosphere holding their negative feelings and private topics, encouraging Free expression, reducing defensiveness and self-blame, promoting trust and openness.
273.when_to_use: In the initial relationship-building phase and throughout, especially when the client states distress, mistakes or sensitive privacy, worries about not being accepted, has low self-evaluation or feels misunderstood.
273.trigger: When the client Self-denies, Low mood or worries about being judged; worries about reputation damage, Relationship tension or self-blame and shame after conflict; expressing Loneliness, low self-esteem, longing for recognition; revealing guilt, loss, sadness and other negative emotions.

264.skill_name: Listen actively and Encouraging full expression
264.skill_description: Focused, uninterrupted Listening to the client's chief complaint and important events, restating key points, Clarification and responding at the right time, encouraging their full expression, grasping thedistress context and meaning in a safe supportive atmosphere, promoting trust and data collection, laying the foundation for subsequent exploration and cooperation.
264.when_to_use: The stage of data collection and emotional expression, running through early assessment and subsequent sessions; entering the narrative stage or the early rapport-building phase; the first session and when expression is restricted.
264.trigger: When the client begins coherently narrating symptoms, events and interpersonal distress; Silence, hesitation or only brief responses; little emotional disclosure, Intellectualization or partial Emotional isolation, needing more companionship and acceptance.

260.skill_name: Accurately Empathy and feed back the client's experience
260.skill_description: Staying focused and patient, listening carefully to narration and capturing helplessness, Fear, sadness and other feelings; putting oneself in their place to experience their feelings and thinking, accurately reflecting core experience and needs in Empathic language, conveying acceptance and attention, enhancing the sense of safety, helping regulate emotions, deepening connection and self-expression.
260.when_to_use: Used throughout, especially early and when talking about family upheavals, important events and painful emotions; in the deepening-relationship and misunderstanding-Clarification phase; during strong emotions or the exploration period of unfinished business.
260.trigger: When the client reveals helplessness, Fear, grief and other strong emotions; talking about breakups, roommate conflicts, adaptation difficulties causing emotional fluctuation; self-reporting 'useless', 'utterly worthless' and other negative evaluations; tension, Anxiety, insomnia or decreased self-efficacy.

300.skill_name: Express encouragement and support and share positive experiences
300.skill_description: When the client makes progress, clearly express encouragement and support, and share the counselor's positive emotional experience on hearing about their growth, consolidating their motivation for change and sense of self-support and enhancing the warmth and mutual trust in the relationship.
300.when_to_use: After the client shows raised awareness, improved relationships or new attempts; when resources and motivation need Reinforcement.
300.trigger: The client reports positive changes such as improved relations with roommates, being able to self-support, or expressing new emotional experiences.

325.skill_name: Continuously give unconditional positive regard and acceptance
325.skill_description: In interaction, continuously responding to the client's experience and choices with non-judgmental acceptance and care, conveying their value is seen and respected, buffering inferiority and Fear of being evaluated, repairing safety and self-worth, so they dare to talk about painful experiences and real needs.
325.when_to_use: Throughout, especially during self-disclosure, sensitive topics or when the client expresses pain, self-blame and worries about being negated; in the relationship-consolidation phase.
325.trigger: When the client is inferior, cares about others' views, fears rejection or abandonment; Anxiety, depression or obsessive symptoms causing pain; self-criticism, fearing being negated; talking about childhood lacking love and attention or being misunderstood and humiliated.

272.skill_name: Communicating with a genuine and congruent attitude
272.skill_description: In interaction, genuinely honest, consistent in words and actions, not pretending, not playing roles; getting along in a natural, sincere way, lowering the client's guardedness, fostering an equal trusting relationship, providing a safe basis for deep exploration and cooperation.
272.when_to_use: At the start of relationship building and maintained throughout; when the relationship is tested or distrust appears.
272.trigger: When the client is sensitive to others' evaluations, inferior and Anxious, or harbors concerns about the counselor's motives.

315.skill_name: Create a safe, warm, accepting expressive environment
315.skill_description: Responding with inclusiveness and understanding, deliberately creating a safe, warm, accepting session atmosphere; through posture and tone, attitude consistency, letting them relax and trust, clearly allowing Free expression and safe exploration, supporting presenting experience in review and rehearsal, lowering defensiveness and guardedness, promoting trust formation and maintenance.
315.when_to_use: The first counseling and relationship-building period; when discussing sensitive topics or when emotional intensity rises; in sessions of difficult expression or emotional catharsis; before and after in-depth exploration.
315.trigger: First-time help-seeking appearing tense and guarded; revealing concerns or tension before/after reviewing unpleasant scenes or Role playing; Repression, self-reported grievance or many negative emotions; revealing tension, worry about being hurt; talking about traumatic evaluations and shame.

252.skill_name: Respond to experience with accurate Empathy and emotional reflection
252.skill_description: When the client has difficulty expressing themselves or their emotions are strong, acknowledge their feelings and difficulty expressing with concrete emotional language; understand empathically and feed back the core emotions and meanings, keenly catch and accurately reflect them, keep the distance of 'as if', avoid rash advice or judgment, help them clarify and own the present emotions, relieving tension and agitation and promoting trust and self-awareness.
252.when_to_use: In early counseling or when the client Regresses, is restless, frequently says 'do not know'; when their emotions are strong, narration vague or Self-denial emotions; when stating negative experiences and emotions, in the exploration phase and when emotions run high.
252.trigger: Little eye contact, tense and irritable, impoverished language or replying 'do not know'; Silence, speechlessness, rationality suppressing emotions or repeatedly emphasizing 'should not'; chest tightness, Anxiety, insomnia, low Learning efficiency; criticized, misunderstood or Fear-contaminated memories; poor sleep, Low mood, interpersonal sensitivity; reddened eyes, helpless exhaustion, pain after being compared and humiliated; tearfully recounting failed elections, interpersonal conflicts and family events.

242.skill_name: Listen patiently and attentively, avoiding interruption
242.skill_description: Give ample time for the client to narrate completely, convey respect and positive regard through focused listening; maintain eye contact and nodding responses, recap and summarize key points at appropriate times, help them sort out their thinking and stabilize emotions, enhance understanding and trust, and support expression and data collection.
242.when_to_use: The assessment and rapport-building stage, especially the first session; the early-relationship stage and the core communication stage of every session; when the client needs to talk things out or when information is being gathered.
242.trigger: When narrating dorm conflicts or growth history, language not fluent, voice quiet, daring not to look directly; needing to be heard when detailing compulsive behaviors and injury experiences; emotional agitation, sighing, tense Anxiety; strong desire to vent, chaotic narration or little eye contact.

249.skill_name: Follow and co-describe the here-and-now experience
249.skill_description: Follow the client and, with concrete description, jointly present their present language, behavior, emotions and bodily sensations; give gentle awareness feedback on the visible clues of the moment, replacing judgment with description, helping them notice and name the experience; after talking about the past, guide them back to the present, concretize the emotions, clarify and raise awareness, creating a space of being understood and accepted.
249.when_to_use: The early session and relationship-building stage; when obvious or subtle emotional and nonverbal changes appear; when building the alliance early on or when the client avoids and defends.
249.trigger: When the client narrates important experiences appearing confused, struggling to grasp feelings; facial expression changing, body tense, slight movement changes, pace and tone changes or voice choking; after narrating key experiences voice softening, avoiding details, watching the counselor's reaction or struggling to describe present discomfort.

299.skill_name: Invite here-and-now expression and staying with feelings
299.skill_description: Invite the client to bring attention back to the scene, become aware of and express the present feelings about the counseling process and the counselor; when an emotional or bodily reaction is noticed, invite them to stay in the current state, carefully feel the bodily sensations and emotions (such as anger, sadness), prompting real interaction to appear, strengthening safety and containment, and supporting real expression and the formation of trust.
299.when_to_use: After the relationship gradually stabilizes or the quality of interaction and here-and-now awareness need to be deepened; when important relationship themes are touched or strong emotions appear.
299.trigger: When the client overly stays in analysis or narration, insufficient emotional expression; having present emotional experiences toward the counselor or process; mentioning key events with rising emotional intensity or bodily tension; struggling to express or wanting to flee present feelings.

233.skill_name: Promptly affirm and concretely Reinforce positive changes and efforts
233.skill_description: Promptly affirm and encourage the client's courage and effort (such as 'it is great that you can actively and bravely explore this'), give concrete, genuine positive feedback and congratulations for their strengths and progress, strengthening confidence and inner motivation and raising cooperation willingness; one may invite them to share experiences of harmonious interaction and study progress, consolidating connection and self-efficacy.
233.when_to_use: After the client completes thinking or offers insights; when clearly making positive choices or taking action; when identifying their strengths, efforts or positive changes; in the consolidation phase and each Session summary.
233.trigger: The client proactively thinking, trying to respond, or carrying out graded classification; expressing positive statements such as 'I have thought it through' and 'make a wise choice'; mentioning their own highlights, completing tasks, or showing progress; after reporting progress, being accepted by peers, or completing established tasks.

291.skill_name: Convey acceptance with a warm, genuine opening and nonverbal behavior
291.skill_description: With a warm tone, focused gaze and present posture, combined with nonverbal behaviors such as smiling, friendly greeting and gesturing to sit down, open with respect, enthusiasm and positive regard, thank and affirm the visit, convey the experience of safety and being valued, lowering tension and defenses, promoting trust building in the initial-visit stage.
291.when_to_use: At the opening of the first consultation and the early stage of relationship building, especially when the client is cautious or tense; at the opening of each session, used to quickly create a safe and warm atmosphere.
291.trigger: When the client has evasive eyes, low voice, slow speech, reserved unease; worried face, Low mood but willing to communicate; tense or confused at first talk; first visit sitting on the front half of the seat, gaze evasive; Silence, resistance or expressing inferiority and worry about being judged.
